drawings.description: une page entière de dessin, au crayon : un cylindre vertical dont le cercle supérieur est marqué $V_{\mathbb{C}}^{\omega}$, le cercle inférieur $V_{\mathbb{C}}^{\omega'}$, et le cercle médian (l'équateur) $V^{\omega}$, chacun avec une flèche de sens de rotation. Sur le cercle supérieur, les points $\tilde P_{a_1}^{\omega}$, $\tilde P_s^{\omega}$, $\tilde P_a^{\omega}$, et l'arc $\tilde d_s^{\omega}$ (un premier libellé biffé) tracé en gras de $\tilde P_{a_1}^{\omega}$ à $\tilde P_a^{\omega}$ ; de $\tilde P_a^{\omega}$ descend en gras un segment vertical, libellé $\tilde c_r$ ou $\tilde c_a^{\omega}$, jusqu'au point $\tilde Q_a$ de l'équateur ; le long de la verticale en pointillé issue de $\tilde P_{a_1}^{\omega}$ on lit $\tilde c_{a_1}^{\omega} = \tilde c_{\omega^{-1}(r_1)}$, et plus bas $\tilde c_{r_1} = \tilde c_{a_1}^{\omega'}$. Sur l'équateur, quatre petits cercles fléchés autour de points marqués (des lacets autour des points enlevés), les points $\tilde Q_{a_1}$, $\tilde R_{r_1}$, $\tilde R_s$, $R_r$, $\tilde Q_a$, les arcs $\tilde b_{r_1}$, $\tilde b_r$ (en gras), et un demi-cercle gras $\tilde a_r$ autour de $\tilde R_s$ ; un triangle hachuré à l'intérieur porte les libellés $r$, $r'$, $r''$, $r_1$, $r_2$, plusieurs autres étant biffés. Sur le cercle inférieur, les points $\tilde P_{a_1}^{\omega'}$, $\tilde P_s^{\omega}$, $\tilde P_a^{\omega'}$, les libellés $(\tilde d_{r_1})$, $\tilde d_{r_1}$ ou $\tilde d_s^{\omega'}$, et l'arc fléché $\tilde b_r^{\omega'}$. Des lettres pâles $a_\omega$, $a$, $a_{\omega'}$ dans la marge gauche du cylindre.
drawings.kind: surface figure (cylinder with marked points, paths and loops)
drawings.notes: Redrawn on the knots read off the crop. The three circles V_C^omega, V^omega, V_C^omega' are closed curves through those knots, and every marked point is one of the knots, so the paths start and end exactly on the circles: P~a1, P~s, P~a on the front of the top circle (the bold arc d~s^omega from P~a1 to P~a, arrow at P~a); the bold c~a^omega from P~a straight down to Q~a; on the equator Q~a1, R~r1, R~s, R~r, Q~a (arrow b~r1 from Q~a1 to R~r1, bold b~r from Q~a to R~r, bold half-circle a~r centred at R~s from R~r to R~r1, its lower half in pencil); on the bottom circle P~a1^omega', P~s, P~a^omega' and the arrow b~r^omega'. The equator runs through five looped points (two on the left, one at the back, two on the right; the transcription says four), each drawn as a circle round the point. The hatched triangle has its apex at one point and its sides end at Q~a1 and Q~a; the pencil line from the lower left loop to the apex bounds the hatched sliver on the left. Front paths (pencil) P~a1 -> Q~a1 -> P~a1^omega' and Q~a -> P~a^omega'; back paths (dotted) from the back of the top circle through the back of the equator to the back of the bottom circle. Orientation arrows: those on the top and bottom circles and the rotation arrow by V_C^omega. Left out: the struck labels (the first d~s, the struck words in the triangle and the long struck stroke to its right), the pale letters a_omega, a, a_omega' in the left margin and the « (r) » cut at the edge, the arrowheads of the small loops and of the equator, the faint line from the apex to the right side. Still differs: the circles are drawn as single closed curves, without his doubled strokes; of the overwritten labels in the triangle only r2, r, r', r'' are kept, r1 (written over r2) is not drawn. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): five small arrowed circles stand on the equator (two on the left, one at the back, two on the right), besides the point R~s with its bold half-circle; the transcription's « quatre » is a miscount. Not checked by a reader.
drawings.disagreement: Five arrowed loops round points of the equator, not four as in the transcription (R~s with its bold half-circle not counted).

drawings.description: Un grand cercle, sur lequel sont marqués et nommés des points : en haut $\widetilde{R}^\omega_k$, $\widetilde{R}_k$, $\widetilde{R}^{\omega'}_k$, puis en tournant $\widetilde{Q}^{\omega'}_j$, $-\widetilde{R}_i$ et ses deux voisins, $\widetilde{Q}^\omega_k$, $\widetilde{R}_j$ et ses deux voisins, $\widetilde{Q}^{\omega'}_i$, en bas $-\widetilde{R}^{\omega'}_k$, $-\widetilde{R}_k$, $-\widetilde{R}^\omega_k$, puis $\widetilde{Q}^\omega_j$, $\widetilde{R}_i$ et ses voisins, $\widetilde{Q}^{\omega'}_k$, $-\widetilde{R}_j$ et ses voisins, $\widetilde{Q}^\omega_i$. Chacun des six points $\pm\widetilde{R}$ est entouré d'un petit demi-cercle ; deux triangles inscrits forment une étoile à six branches, et quelques traits au crayon partent du centre et vers l'extérieur.
drawings.notes: Circle with 18 named points: six triples ±R~ (R~^omega, R~, R~^omega') each with a small half-circle round the middle point, and six Q~ between them; the two inscribed triangles join R~_k, R~_i, R~_j and -R~_k, -R~_i, -R~_j (pencil). Pencil strokes from the centre and towards the outside drawn as seen; the far end of the long stroke at the bottom right (a dot) is kept. Labels placed after the transcription.

drawings.description: Page de figures, sans texte suivi. En haut, un cercle avec une flèche courbe notée $3$ (rotation d'ordre 3), deux triangles inscrits, des points marqués de part et d'autre des sommets et étiquetés de petits symboles $R$, $Q$ avec exposants $2$, $3$, $\bar 3$ (illisibles dans le détail) ; des tirets vont d'un sommet vers le centre. En bas à gauche, une sphère avec équateur et méridien, les points $Q_+$ (en haut), $Q_-$ (en bas), $P_+$, $Q_0$, $P'$ sur l'équateur, avec de petites boucles autour de certains points. Au milieu, une petite ellipse et un petit cercle partagé en trois. En bas à droite, un tétraèdre, une flèche, puis une sphère traversée par une ellipse avec des flèches tangentes.
drawings.kind: page of figures (circle with triangles, sphere, sketches)
drawings.notes: Top: the circle and the two inscribed triangles, every vertex placed on the circle (projected from the crop) and every side drawn between the same vertices; the two dashed strokes from the upper right and the right vertex end at one centre point (arrowhead there); the seven heavy dots and the six small ticks on the circle, all on it; the rotation arrow marked 3. Bottom left: the sphere outline (pencil), the dashed circle through Q+ and Q- (both points on it), the equator drawn straight through P+, Q0 and P', the meridian as a narrow ellipse (front solid, back pencil, his bold bits at the top and bottom), the three small loops, and the small oval with its dot at the left edge. Middle: the small ellipse with three dots and its short spoke; the small circle with its three spokes from one inner point (top, lower left, lower right) and a fourth faint spoke to the left (pencil). Bottom right: the tetrahedron (AC bold, BD dashed), the arrow, the sphere crossed by the narrow ellipse, the two long vertical arrows along it and the four short tangent arrows. Still differs: the small labels round the top circle (R, Q with exponents 2, 3, 3bar, read as illegible in detail by the transcription) are left out; the labels Q+ / Q- follow the transcription (on the crop the top one may read Q with a bar); the sphere at the bottom right is faint and its long arrows are approximate; scanner shadow ignored. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (maths): the sign by the top pole is a bare horizontal dash, raised like the + of P+ on the left, so it is a minus and not a plus; the two poles being the pair Q+, Q-, the top one is Q- and the bottom one Q+ (its sign is merged with the point). The two labels are exchanged in the redraw. Not checked by a reader.
drawings.disagreement: On the sphere at the lower left the top pole is labelled Q with a minus sign (a bare dash) and the bottom pole Q+; the transcription has them the other way round.

drawings.description: Une chaîne de points sur une courbe fermée, chacun muni de petites boucles fléchées (les lacets $\lambda$), reliés par des flèches à double sens. Au premier plan, en trait gras : $\widetilde{Q}_a \xrightarrow{\tilde b_r} \widetilde{R}_r$, puis un arc $\tilde a_r$ de $\widetilde{R}_r$ vers $\widetilde{R}_{r_1}$, sous lequel un arc $\tilde a_{r_1}$ ; au-dessus, un autre point avec l'arc $\tilde a_{r_1^\vee}$. La région entre $\widetilde{R}_r$, $\widetilde{Q}_a$ et un sommet commun est hachurée ; des traits fins portent $r$, $r_1$, $r_2$. Plus bas à droite, un petit triangle isolé.
drawings.kind: surface figure (chain of looped points, paths)
drawings.notes: Closed chain of five looped points: each loop is a circle round its point, and the double arrows run along the straight segments between the points (top <-> top right, top <-> upper left, upper left <-> lower left as a curve on the left, top right <-> lower right as a curve on the right). From the lower left point the chain goes through the dot to R~r1 (arrows), from Q~a to the lower right point (arrow). The bold b~r runs from Q~a to R~r, the bold a~r is the upper half of an ellipse from R~r to R~r1 (arrow at R~r1), the thin a~r1 its lower half, so the two arcs share their end points. The hatched region is bounded by the line from the apex to the right, the arc a~r and the vertical from the apex; the faint lines from the apex to the lower left point and to the dot are drawn in pencil, with r, r1, r2 by them. Left out: the long horizontal rule across the top (a stroke of the page, not of the figure), the label above the top loop written on that rule (« a~r » with a mark? not certain), the arrowheads of the small loops, the small isolated triangle lower right (outside the bbox). The label a~_{r1^vee} is placed under the top loop, where « a r1 » with a check mark stands. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: un hexagone inscrit dans un cercle, de sommets marqués $\tilde{R}_1$, $\tilde{R}'_0$, $\tilde{R}_5$, $\tilde{R}'_4$, $\tilde{R}_3$, $\tilde{R}_2$ (ce dernier surchargé d'un $4$), le centre pointé ; les diagonales et quelques cordes sont tracées en tirets au crayon.
drawings.notes: Hexagon inscribed in a pencil circle, centre pointed. The dashed chords are a reading of scattered pencil dashes: the six drawn here (R1-R3, R'0-R'4, R1-R5, R'0-R3, R2-R'4, R3-R5) are those whose dashes line up; others may be intended. The R~2 label is overwritten by a 4 (kept as R~2, as in the transcription).

drawings.description: en haut à gauche, une sphère portant un grand cercle (équateur) avec quatre petits cercles pointés ; légende « 4 sommets, deux faces ». Une flèche « deux façons » mène à une seconde sphère, même équateur à quatre sommets cerclés, coupé par un grand cercle méridien (« cercle marqué ») ; légende « 1 cercle marqué, 6 sommets, 4 faces ».
drawings.notes: Two spheres: equator with four ringed vertices; then the same cut by a marked great circle (meridian). Encoded as cellular/1; his counts (4 sommets, deux faces; 6 sommets, 4 faces) are reproduced. The legends under the figures (« 3 possibilités pour I », « 6 possibilités pour I ») are text of the transcription and are not redrawn.

drawings.description: une flèche vers le haut, marquée « trois façons (supprimer une des trois \struck{\ill{}} d'arêtes opposées) », part d'un tétraèdre dont les quatre sommets portent de petits angles ; légende « 4 sommets, 4 faces ». À droite, une petite sphère au crayon et un croquis raturé (une sphère quadrillée dans un cube), avec « \struck{\ill{}} I ».
drawings.notes: Upward arrow (its legend « trois façons (supprimer une des trois paires d'arêtes opposées) » is text of the transcription, not redrawn), tetrahedron with small angle marks at the vertices, legend « 4 sommets, 4 faces ». The small pencil sphere at the right is drawn in pencil grey. Omitted as struck: the sketch scribbled over below it (a gridded sphere in a cube) and its struck label « [ill] I ». Issue 128, 2026-11-09: struck material left out after a fresh check of the facsimile (struck-out material is not drawn). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: sous un trait horizontal, deux sphères. À gauche, « I », avec le schéma de trois branches « $\vee\!\!\!\perp\!\vee$ » : équateur à cinq sommets cerclés, coupé par deux grands cercles méridiens ; « $\mathbb{Z}/2$ » ; légende « $9 = 5 + 4$ sommets, \struck{\ill{}} faces, deux cercles marqués » et « $12.5 = 60$ possibilités pour $K$ (pentagone + sommet) », « $D_{01}$ ». À droite, « II », schéma « $\vee\!\!\perp\!\vee$ » : équateur à cinq sommets cerclés, un méridien ; « $\mathbb{Z}/2$ » ; légende « $5 + 2 = 7$ sommets, 4 faces, 1 cercle marqué » et « $12.5 = 60$ poss.\ \uncertain{pour} \ill{} (pentagone + arête) », « $D_{02}$ ».
drawings.kind: cell decomposition of the sphere (two cases)
drawings.notes: I: equator with five ringed vertices cut by two disjoint marked circles (each meets the equator twice): encoded V=9 (5+4, as he writes), E=13, F=6 -- his face count is struck and illegible, the encoding gives 6. II: equator with five ringed vertices and one marked meridian: V=7, F=4 as he writes. The three-branch schemas are given as text (as in the transcription), not redrawn stroke by stroke. Exact order of the crossings among the ringed vertices read from the figure; it does not affect the counts.

drawings.description: à gauche, « III » : une sphère portant deux cercles parallèles reliés par deux montants verticaux, le cercle du haut « cercle marqué », deux sommets cerclés sur le cercle du bas et deux au pôle ; « $\mathbb{Z}/2$ » ; légende « $9 = 3 + 3 + 1 + 2$ sommets, 6 faces, 1 cercle marqué » ; « $60 = 10 \times 3 \times 2$ poss.\ pour $K$ » ; « (triangle + sommet marqué + \ill{}) » avec sous les termes 10, 3, 2. Au centre, un schéma en « $\vee\!\!\perp\!\vee$ » à deux branches. À droite : « $D_0$ », « III » : une sphère à équateur portant cinq sommets cerclés, marquée « $D_5$ » ; légende « \struck{12 façons} 5 sommets, 2 faces, 12 possibilités qui \ill{} orientation de $K$ » ; « IV », « $D_2$ » : une sphère méridienne en fuseaux avec trois sommets cerclés ; légende « \struck{\ill{}} sommets, 6 faces, 20 possibilités (cf \ill{}, car il faut choisir une orientation de la sphère) $\sim$ orientation de $K$ » ; un croquis raturé « $\mathfrak{S}_3$ ».
drawings.kind: cell decompositions of the sphere (page of cases)
drawings.notes: III (left): the two parallel circles (back halves dashed), the two posts from the front of the top circle to the two ringed vertices on the front of the bottom circle, all their end points computed on the ellipses; the pole: a solid stroke from the front centre of the top circle to the ringed vertex on its back, the hook up to the second ringed vertex, the dotted stroke from there down through the back of the top circle to the ringed vertex on the back of the bottom circle, beside it the inked (filled) ring; the faint pencil axis and the faint sphere outline. His count « 9 = 3+3+1+2 sommets, 6 faces » is NOT encoded: the figure alone does not fix where the 3+3+1+2 vertices sit. The V-bar-V schema in the middle: a V and a three-pronged fork joined by a bar. D0 / D5 (right, top): the equator with five ringed vertices on it (projected onto the ellipse), encoded (V = 5, E = 5, F = 2, as he writes). IV / D2: four meridians from one top point to one bottom point, the front of the equator, the two ringed vertices on it and the third between the two middle meridians -- redrawn only (his vertex count is struck). The legends are copied as the transcription reads them, at \small. Left out (struck in the original): the struck S3 sketch at the bottom, the struck « 12 façons » and the struck vertex count of IV. Also left out: the loose dots and the forked segment along the bottom edge of the bbox (they belong to the text below). Still differs: the meridians of D2 are drawn as smooth curves, without his doubled strokes; the faint sphere top right is approximate. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: en bas, plusieurs croquis largement raturés : une ellipse, une sphère en fuseaux à quatre sommets cerclés (« $9 = 5 + 4\,\struck{+1}$ sommets », « 30 possibilités (car il faut choisir l'orientation du carré) »), une petite sphère à quatre sommets, un tétraèdre, une sphère « $D_1$ » ; flèches « $\to D_1$ », « $\mathbb{Z}$ ». À gauche, une liste :
drawings.notes: Strike-outs are not drawn (issue 128). Struck in the original and left out: the ellipse (crossed by a zigzag), the sphere in lunes with four ringed vertices (crossed by long diagonal strokes), the tetrahedron (crossed by a zigzag) and the sphere at the bottom right (scribbled over), the « +1 » of « 9 = 5 + 4 + 1 sommets ». Drawn: the small sphere with its top vertex and four ringed vertices on the equator (back half pencil), joined to the top vertex by four arcs; the arrow « -> D1 », the second arrow with « Z » as the transcription reads it (the « Z » may be the start of the zigzag over the tetrahedron), the legends « 9 = 5 + 4 sommets », « 30 possibilités (car il faut choisir l'orientation du carré) », which are not struck, and the label D1 at the right, which belonged to the struck sphere. The list on the left (D0 -> D1 ...) is text, carried by the transcription. Still differs: the small sphere's arcs are smooth curves read by eye; whether its outline is closed at the lower right is unclear. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page): the ellipse and the tetrahedron are each crossed by a zigzag, the sphere in lunes by long oblique strokes and the bottom right sphere by a scribble: all four are struck and stay left out. The sign after the arrows is a heavy Z with a doubled stroke, in a heavier pen than the thin zigzag over the tetrahedron and apart from it: a letter, kept. Not checked by a reader.

drawings.description: En tête de page, plusieurs croquis : un octaèdre (ou double pyramide) aux faces hachurées ; un triangle avec un petit triangle intérieur ; deux triangles réunis par un sommet (« nœud papillon ») ; un triangle marqué $+$, avec au-dessous un segment et un triangle aux sommets $0$, $1$, $\infty$.
drawings.notes: Octahedron / double pyramid with two hatched faces (its apex touches the top edge of the bbox); a triangle with a small inner triangle; the bow-tie (two triangles sharing a vertex); a triangle marked + with an inner vertex, a segment with three points, and the triangle 0, 1, infinity (only its strokes; the labels are placed from the transcription, their exact attribution to the corners uncertain). A small mark under the second triangle (a « 4 »?) is not read and left out.

drawings.description: Dans la colonne de gauche, trois sphères : la première porte un cercle équatorial avec cinq points marqués ; la deuxième un sommet au pôle relié par des arcs à quatre points de l'équateur ; la troisième des cercles méridiens et un axe pointillé, avec des points marqués aux pôles et sur l'équateur.
drawings.notes: Three spheres. 1: equator with five ringed points. 2: a ringed pole joined by four arcs (one dashed, behind) to four ringed points of the equator. 3: meridian circles, dotted polar axis, ringed points at both poles, at the centre and at both ends of the equator -- redrawn but not encoded (the number of meridians is not certain: two are clearly drawn). He gives no counts here, so the encodings are checked only for Euler (chi = 2). Text in the left margin (Z/5Z, D5 ...) belongs to the transcription.

drawings.description: En haut à gauche, un polyèdre en perspective formé de deux faces pentagonales (arêtes pleines et pointillées), les arêtes marquées $a, b, c, d, e$ et $a', b', c', d', e'$ ; une flèche courbe près de $b'$.
drawings.notes: Front pentagon (bold) with a dot on each side (a-e), every side drawn between the same five computed vertices and the dots placed at points of the sides. To its right, the inner vertex joined to the two right vertices (d', c'), the outer vertex joined to them (e', b'), the thin stroke from the upper right vertex to the point where the outer stroke b' meets the small triangle at the bottom right (computed on that stroke), the two long strokes leaving the upper and lower right vertices, the bold curved arrow by b', and the pencil arc under the side e. Behind (dashed), the strokes he made in dashes, as read: from the upper left vertex and from the dot c to a back point (dotted e'), from there to a second back point, from the left vertex to that point, on to a third back point (dotted b'') and down to the lower left vertex; from the dot c to the dot d and from d to the third back point. Not encoded: the dashed strokes are scattered dashes and their joins are a reading, so they do not fix a polyhedron (prism? half a dodecahedron?). Still differs: the dashed joins are a reading; his doubled side d is drawn once; the label by the third back point reads b'' or b'. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: Une série de sphères portant des points cerclés sur l'équateur et aux pôles, reliés par des arcs méridiens, étiquetées : $D_{01}$ ; $D_{12}$ (deux sphères) ; $D_0$ (cinq points sur un cercle équatorial, une flèche, signe $+$) ; $D_1$ (un pôle relié à quatre points de l'équateur, avec la mention « $(+\circlearrowleft)$ ») ; \struck{$D_2$} $D_2$ (sphère marquée $+$ et $-$).
drawings.kind: cell decompositions of the sphere (series D01, D12, D0, D1, D2)
drawings.notes: Five small spheres; on each, the ringed points are placed on the equator ellipse (projected) and every meridian ends at a ringed point. D01: four ringed points on the equator, the ringed top point joined to the front right one (solid) and, by a faint stroke read as reaching it, to the back right one (pencil). D12: the second sphere, with top and bottom points, two ringed points on the front of the equator joined to both poles, a ringed point on the back half (dashed) and the cross on the front, on the dashed axis from the top. D0 (five ringed points on the equator, the arrow, +) and D1 (the ringed pole joined to four ringed points of the equator, « (+ ↺) ») are encoded (cellular/1: V5 E5 F2 and V5 E8 F5, chi = 2; he gives no counts). D2: the axis through the central ring, the two side meridians broken at the equator as he draws them, + and -. Left out, struck in the original: the first D12 sphere (crossed by long diagonal strokes), the first label D2, the inked sign before « (+ ↺) » and the squiggle by « - ». Still differs: D01, D12 and D2 are redrawn, not encoded (their meridians are partly broken or faint, so the figure does not fix the cells); his doubled outlines are drawn once. The top strip of the crop belongs to 04-3. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Revised 2026-11-11 after Michel's check (#142): confirmed as redrawn.

drawings.description: Dans la moitié inférieure : un petit triangle hachuré ; un icosaèdre en perspective dont les arêtes portent les lettres $a, b, c, d, e$ ; un grand patron déplié de faces (pentagones et quadrilatères) aux arêtes marquées $a, \ldots, e$, avec des flèches courbes indiquant des recollements ; à droite, trois sphères au crayon portant des points cerclés et des méridiens.
drawings.kind: polyhedron net (pentagons and quadrilaterals), icosahedron sketch, spheres
drawings.notes: Redrawn stroke by stroke on computed vertices: every stroke of the net and of the small icosahedron is drawn between named vertices shared by the strokes that meet there. Icosahedron sketch (top left): the top spike, the outer and inner top vertices, the left, right and bottom vertices and the strokes between them as he drew them, the dots on the edges placed on those edges, the crosses at the left, and his edge letters a-e where they can be read. Small hatched triangle at the top, with the two faint strokes near it (pencil). The net: the central pentagon (sides a, d, e, b and the doubled left side), the inner vertex joined to the bottom right vertex, to the letter in the middle and up to the right (e); on the left the quadrilaterals (b, a, d, d, e), above them the faces through e, b (dotted) and d, the long faint vertical to the top of the pentagon and the faint strokes on the left (pencil), on the right the strokes towards a vertex beyond the crop edge (a, c); the five curved gluing arrows and the dotted one; the edge letters as they stand. Three pencil spheres at the right with their ringed points on the equators (projected) and meridians ending at the poles; the lowest has the bold axis and the dashed meridian. Not encoded: the net is faint and overdrawn, so which edges are glued cannot be fixed from the figure alone. Still differs: the faces of the net are a reading of overdrawn pencil (his doubled strokes drawn once, some faint strokes beyond the drawn vertices left out); the heavy letter in the middle of the net (« S » or « 5 »?) and the faint erased letters inside the pentagon are left out; the letters on the icosahedron are placed as read, some uncertain. Top right: the lune s-t with c, d, b, e, the chord through alpha (dashed beyond), the hatched region. drawings.description: tableau de graphes, une ligne par type $(g,\nu)$, avec à droite de chaque ligne un nombre qui est vraisemblablement la dimension $3g-3+\nu$. Dans chaque ligne, les graphes MD du type sont dessinés (sommets marqués de leur genre quand il est non nul, arêtes libres en flèches sortantes), reliés par des flèches de spécialisation dirigées vers les graphes plus simples, certaines affectées d'une multiplicité ($2$, $3$). $(0,3)$ : un sommet à trois arêtes libres ; nombre $0$. $(0,4)$ : le sommet à quatre arêtes libres $\leftarrow$ deux sommets trivalents joints par une arête ; nombre $1$. $(0,5)$ : sommet à cinq arêtes libres $\leftarrow$ deux sommets $\xleftarrow{2}$ trois sommets en chaîne ; nombre $2$. $(0,6)$ : sommet à six arêtes libres, puis graphes à deux, trois et quatre sommets, dont une étoile à trois branches, avec flèches marquées $2$ et $3$ ; nombre $3$. $(1,1)$ : un sommet de genre $1$ à une arête libre $\leftarrow$ une boucle à une arête libre ; nombre $1$. $(1,2)$ : sommet de genre $1$ à deux arêtes libres, puis boucle à deux arêtes libres, sommet de genre $1$ relié à un sommet trivalent, deux sommets joints par une double arête, etc., flèche marquée $2$ ; nombre $2$. $(1,3)$ : diagramme analogue, plus touffu, aboutissant à un triangle à trois arêtes libres, flèches marquées $2$ et $3$ ; nombre $3$. $(2,0)$ : sommet de genre $2$ ; sommet de genre $1$ à une boucle ; deux sommets de genre $1$ joints par une arête ; sommet de genre $1$ relié à une boucle ; huit (deux boucles en un sommet) ; deux sommets joints par trois arêtes ; flèches marquées $2$, $3$ et une flèche marquée d'un signe peu lisible ; nombre $3$. $(2,1)$ : premiers graphes seulement, puis « ……… » ; nombre $4$.

drawings.notes: Encoded and rendered canonically, not traced: for each row the stable graphs of type (g, nu) with unlabelled legs are enumerated by program (comb.enumerate_stable) and compared with the number he draws. Counts agree for (0,3) 1, (0,4) 2, (0,5) 3, (0,6) 7, (1,1) 2, (1,2) 5, (2,0) 7 (the 7 strata of M2-bar) and, re-counted on the crop, (1,3) 11 (two of them overinked), which the program also finds; (2,1): 16 exist, he draws the first 3 (genus-2 vertex with a leg; genus-1 vertex with a loop and a leg; two genus-1 vertices joined by an edge, with the leg under a scribble) and breaks off with « ……… » -- those 3 are rendered (the earlier rendering had dropped the third). His number at the right of each row equals 3g - 3 + nu in every row (0,1,2,3,1,2,3,3,4). Labels at \small. Still differs, and why it stays partial: the specialisation arrows between graphs and their multiplicities (2, 3, one illegible sign) are NOT encoded, so the rendering shows the graphs, not the arrows, and its layout is canonical (vertices on a line), so it does not lay over the page.
